blocks.text: Dohra:

Now listen to the episode about S. Shyam Singh1 , Who became the supreme chief among the Misl chiefs. Revered Guru Gobind Singh had blessed him, When, as a child, had he gone with his father to the Guru. (1)
lines: Now listen to the episode about S.
Shyam Singh1 ,
Who became the supreme chief among the Misl chiefs.
Revered Guru Gobind Singh had blessed him,
When, as a child, had he gone with his father to the Guru.

blocks.text: Chaupai:
Listen to the account about S. Shyam Singh, As I had heard it from my own mother. As Shyam Singh'sdaughter happened to be my mother, So had I (the author) come to know about Shyam Singh (2)
lines: Listen to the account about S.
Shyam Singh,
As I had heard it from my own mother.
As Shyam Singh'sdaughter happened to be my mother,
So had I (the author) come to know about Shyam Singh

blocks.text: There was one person Mali2 , a Sandhu Jat at village Narla, Shyamu amd Mehro were names of his two sons. Majority of the inhabitants being followers of Sultani sect3 then, Shyamu was born there on some auspicious moment. (3)
lines: There was one person Mali2 , a Sandhu Jat at village Narla,
Shyamu amd Mehro were names of his two sons.
Majority of the inhabitants being followers of Sultani sect3 then,
Shyamu was born there on some auspicious moment.

blocks.text: As this grown up child felt very enthusiastic, Hastily did he run to join the Khalsa Panth. As he paid his obeisance at S. Mastan Singh's4 seminary, The latter received him with open arms as his disciple. (4)
lines: As this grown up child felt very enthusiastic,
Hastily did he run to join the Khalsa Panth.
As he paid his obeisance at S.
Mastan Singh's4 seminary,
The latter received him with open arms as his disciple.

blocks.text: Him did Mastan Singh initiate into the Khalsa Panth, Who himself had been initiated by the Five Beloved Singhs5 . As these five beloved Singhs had been initiated by the Guru himself, He, too, had imbibed their divine attributes and prowess. (5)
lines: Him did Mastan Singh initiate into the Khalsa Panth,
Who himself had been initiated by the Five Beloved Singhs5 .
As these five beloved Singhs had been initiated by the Guru himself,
He, too, had imbibed their divine attributes and prowess.

blocks.text: Dohra:

S. Mastan Singh6 had had the privilege to enjoy, The divine company of revered Guru Gobind Singh. As the Guru had sent him in the company of Banda Bahadur7 , So well-known and famous did he become in the world. (6)
lines: S.
Mastan Singh6 had had the privilege to enjoy,
The divine company of revered Guru Gobind Singh.
As the Guru had sent him in the company of Banda Bahadur7 ,
So well-known and famous did he become in the world.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Him had Banda Bahadur appointed an army commander, Martyrdom had he achieved after a fight with the Mughals. Thereafter, had Shyam Singh taken over the Sikh seminary, He, being a relation and a beloved disciple of Mastan Singh. (7)
lines: Him had Banda Bahadur appointed an army commander,
Martyrdom had he achieved after a fight with the Mughals.
Thereafter, had Shyam Singh taken over the Sikh seminary,
He, being a relation and a beloved disciple of Mastan Singh.

blocks.text: Shyam Singh rose to be a very capable and worthy successor, Many a battle did he fight against the Mughals. This is the distinguishing hallmark of Khalsa Singhs, That they always remain on the forefront during fighting. (8)
lines: Shyam Singh rose to be a very capable and worthy successor,
Many a battle did he fight against the Mughals.
This is the distinguishing hallmark of Khalsa Singhs,
That they always remain on the forefront during fighting.

blocks.text: Moreover, they share whatever they partake themselves, Polite of tongue, steadfast do they remain in Sikh code of conduct. To the Gurbani do they remain completely devoted, Day and night do they remain prepared for war. (9)
lines: Moreover, they share whatever they partake themselves,
Polite of tongue, steadfast do they remain in Sikh code of conduct.
To the Gurbani do they remain completely devoted,
Day and night do they remain prepared for war.

blocks.text: If an alien ever paid a visit to their camp, Into a Singh did they convert him after initiation. If he was a Hindu they shared their food with him, With a loving care did they look after the downtrodden. (10)
lines: If an alien ever paid a visit to their camp,
Into a Singh did they convert him after initiation.
If he was a Hindu they shared their food with him,
With a loving care did they look after the downtrodden.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Those Singhs who travelled from the Majha region, They would usually put up with S. Shyam Singh. With open arms would Shyam Singh welcome them, Nothing would he expect from his guests in return. (11)
lines: Those Singhs who travelled from the Majha region,
They would usually put up with S.
Shyam Singh.
With open arms would Shyam Singh welcome them,
Nothing would he expect from his guests in return.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Whatever provisions he had, readily would he share with others, Being short of provisions, never would he feed himself alone. This had been the (golden) tradition among the Khalsa Panth, Never would a Singh eat alone without sharing with others. (12)
lines: Whatever provisions he had, readily would he share with others,
Being short of provisions, never would he feed himself alone.
This had been the (golden) tradition among the Khalsa Panth,
Never would a Singh eat alone without sharing with others.

blocks.text: Whatever one had he would share it with everyone, Having run short of provisions gladly would they call it quits. After feeding one's colleagues would a Singh eat, With feelings of fraternal regards would a Singh entreat others. (13)
lines: Whatever one had he would share it with everyone,
Having run short of provisions gladly would they call it quits.
After feeding one's colleagues would a Singh eat,
With feelings of fraternal regards would a Singh entreat others.

blocks.text: Dohra:

At a time when there occurred a rift, Between Baba Banda Bahadur and Tat Khalsa Singhs8 . The Tat Khalsa Singhs, putting up a camp at Amritsar, Sustained themselves through looting and plundering the Mughals. (14)
lines: At a time when there occurred a rift,
Between Baba Banda Bahadur and Tat Khalsa Singhs8 .
The Tat Khalsa Singhs, putting up a camp at Amritsar,
Sustained themselves through looting and plundering the Mughals.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

When S. Kapoor Singh9 came to be conferred with Nawabship, He made S. Shyam Singh a shareholder in power. Those who had joined Shyam Singh's camp at that time, All of them became Misl chiefs of good repute. (15)
lines: When S.
Kapoor Singh9 came to be conferred with Nawabship,
He made S.
Shyam Singh a shareholder in power.
Those who had joined Shyam Singh's camp at that time,
All of them became Misl chiefs of good repute.

blocks.text: If the (author) narrated the names and addresses of those chiefs, Their number would cross the one thousand mark. Twelve thousand horse-mounted soldiers did he command, Many defectors from other Misls had he enlisted in his Misl. (16)
lines: If the (author) narrated the names and addresses of those chiefs,
Their number would cross the one thousand mark.
Twelve thousand horse-mounted soldiers did he command,
Many defectors from other Misls had he enlisted in his Misl.

blocks.text: First of all, S. Shyam Singh picked up S. Sukha Singh10 of Mari Kambo, Appointed him as the chief custodian of his Misl. S. Sukha Singh died while fighting against Ahmed Shah Abdali, As detailed account of his exploits had already been narrated. (17)
lines: First of all,
S.
Shyam Singh picked up S.
Sukha Singh10 of Mari Kambo,
Appointed him as the chief custodian of his Misl.
S.
Sukha Singh died while fighting against Ahmed Shah Abdali,
As detailed account of his exploits had already been narrated.

blocks.text: S. Karam Singh of Paijgarh succeeded S. Sukha Singh's command, He was a Singh from the Sareen sub-caste of Kshtriyas. He had the guts to capture the Shah-e-Pir of Chittiwaley, He had died after killing a Muslim warrior Khairey Shah" . (18)
lines: S.
Karam Singh of Paijgarh succeeded S.
Sukha Singh's command,
He was a Singh from the Sareen sub-caste of Kshtriyas.
He had the guts to capture the Shah-e-Pir of Chittiwaley,
He had died after killing a Muslim warrior Khairey Shah" .

blocks.text: Dohra:

After Karam Singh,Shyam Singh appointed S. Karora Singh12 , As the chief custodian to command his Misl. He belonged to the Sandhu sub caste among Jats, He happened to be an inhabitant of the Majha region. (19)
lines: After Karam Singh,Shyam Singh appointed S.
Karora Singh12 ,
As the chief custodian to command his Misl.
He belonged to the Sandhu sub caste among Jats,
He happened to be an inhabitant of the Majha region.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Much did this misl gain in strength under Karora Singh's command, A leading misl did it become among the Dal Khalsa forces. Whenever a Singh was turned out by his own Misl, Readily would Karora Singh enlist him in his own Misl. (20)
lines: Much did this misl gain in strength under Karora Singh's command,
A leading misl did it become among the Dal Khalsa forces.
Whenever a Singh was turned out by his own Misl,
Readily would Karora Singh enlist him in his own Misl.

blocks.text: The Bhangi Kalsia Singhs13 whom the Majhail Singhs had turned out, They along with Buria14 and Chhachhrauli15 Singhs were enlisted by Karora Singh. When this Khalsa Misl had marched towards Delhi in 1822 (B.S.) At Tarauri16 did Karora Singh die after a bullet injury. (21)
lines: The Bhangi Kalsia Singhs13 whom the Majhail Singhs had turned out,
They along with Buria14 and Chhachhrauli15 Singhs were enlisted by Karora Singh.
When this Khalsa Misl had marched towards Delhi in 1822 (B.S.) At Tarauri16 did Karora Singh die after a bullet injury.

blocks.text: He was succeeded by his disciple S. Baghel Singh Dhaliwal17 , He was a resident of village Jhabbal from Majha region. A great warrior and a great philanthropist was he, A great conqueror with a gentle demeaneur was he. (22)
lines: He was succeeded by his disciple S.
Baghel Singh Dhaliwal17 ,
He was a resident of village Jhabbal from Majha region.
A great warrior and a great philanthropist was he,
A great conqueror with a gentle demeaneur was he.

blocks.text: A commander of the Karorasingha Misl was he made, As S.Shyam Singh remained the Misl's chief commander. S. Baghel Singh having been made the Misl custodian, Thus did he become the chief among the Misl chiefs. (23)
lines: A commander of the Karorasingha Misl was he made,
As S.Shyam Singh remained the Misl's chief commander.
S.
Baghel Singh having been made the Misl custodian,
Thus did he become the chief among the Misl chiefs.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Kroresinghia Misl was the biggest in the Majha region, It also had territorial rights over one fourth of Doaba. From the foot hills of Doaba region upto the Ganges, This Misl would collect revenues without any hindrance. (24)
lines: Kroresinghia Misl was the biggest in the Majha region,
It also had territorial rights over one fourth of Doaba.
From the foot hills of Doaba region upto the Ganges,
This Misl would collect revenues without any hindrance.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

If any one dared to harass Kroresinghia Misl's Singh, With a dash wouldS. Baghel Singh throw him out. As all the Sikh Misls belonged to the Khalsa Panth, Each Misl had tried their mettle against this Misl. (25)
lines: If any one dared to harass Kroresinghia Misl's Singh,
With a dash wouldS.
Baghel Singh throw him out.
As all the Sikh Misls belonged to the Khalsa Panth,
Each Misl had tried their mettle against this Misl.

blocks.text: Once the Singhs from Malwa region became very arrogant, Though they had made many family relationships in Majha. S. Baghel Singh's Misl stopped their entry in his area, As they wished to take ransom from this Misl. (26)
lines: Once the Singhs from Malwa region became very arrogant,
Though they had made many family relationships in Majha.
S.
Baghel Singh's Misl stopped their entry in his area,
As they wished to take ransom from this Misl.

blocks.text: They laid their hands on Baghel Singh's Misl's territory as well, Forcibly did they occupy the Manimajra in his territory. Even as S. Baghel Singh kept on persuading them to behave, Defiantly did they collect revenues from Behlolpur. (27)
lines: They laid their hands on Baghel Singh's Misl's territory as well,
Forcibly did they occupy the Manimajra in his territory.
Even as S.
Baghel Singh kept on persuading them to behave,
Defiantly did they collect revenues from Behlolpur.

blocks.text: Then did S. Baghel Singh invade with the beatof a drum, Immediately did he ransack Jasla and Sidhna villages. Wth many a villager from the surrounding areas joining him, Strongly did he picket around the Patiala fort. (28)
lines: Then did S.
Baghel Singh invade with the beatof a drum,
Immediately did he ransack Jasla and Sidhna villages.
Wth many a villager from the surrounding areas joining him,
Strongly did he picket around the Patiala fort.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As S. Amar Singh18 got the news about this development, Hardly did he feel alarmed in his heart. He bragged that as he attacked with his massive army, Definitely would he occupy whole of Baghel Singh's territory. (29)
lines: As S.
Amar Singh18 got the news about this development,
Hardly did he feel alarmed in his heart.
He bragged that as he attacked with his massive army,
Definitely would he occupy whole of Baghel Singh's territory.

blocks.text: With many an initiative did he organise his army, Many a messenger did he despatch to invite support. To all his relatives and acquaintances did he ask, Must all of them reach his fort at the earliest. (30)
lines: With many an initiative did he organise his army,
Many a messenger did he despatch to invite support.
To all his relatives and acquaintances did he ask,
Must all of them reach his fort at the earliest.

blocks.text: All the fraternal Phulkian19 feudal chiefs reached, So did his relations of Bhai20 dynasty arrive soon. The Rai Mian of Jagraon too did rush to rally round him, After making a strategic deal with the rulers of Malerkotla. (31)
lines: All the fraternal Phulkian19 feudal chiefs reached,
So did his relations of Bhai20 dynasty arrive soon.
The Rai Mian of Jagraon too did rush to rally round him,
After making a strategic deal with the rulers of Malerkotla.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As S. Paakhar Singh Manshahia arrived with a massive force, So did S. Maha Singh came in a body from Mudki. These two feudal chiefs being Amar Singh's brothers-in-law, They were deployed to lead the massive force from the front. (32)
lines: As S.
Paakhar Singh Manshahia arrived with a massive force,
So did S.
Maha Singh came in a body from Mudki.
These two feudal chiefs being Amar Singh's brothers-in-law,
They were deployed to lead the massive force from the front.

blocks.text: A big force did the Nahan chief bring from Nahan, Whom S. Amar Singh had made his brother through exchange of turbans. Chiefs of Mehraj and Saboki Talwandi did arrive with a force, Along with them came the Kaleke, Gill and Maur chiefs. (33)
lines: A big force did the Nahan chief bring from Nahan,
Whom S.
Amar Singh had made his brother through exchange of turbans.
Chiefs of Mehraj and Saboki Talwandi did arrive with a force,
Along with them came the Kaleke,
Gill and Maur chiefs.

blocks.text: Soon did the Singhpuria chiefs arrive at Amar Singh's support, With whom had they entered into several written deals. And all the petty chiefs from the surrounding areas, Arrived along with all those idlers who had nothing to do. (34)
lines: Soon did the Singhpuria chiefs arrive at Amar Singh's support,
With whom had they entered into several written deals.
And all the petty chiefs from the surrounding areas,
Arrived along with all those idlers who had nothing to do.

blocks.text: Many other sycophants and distant relatives too arrived, All sorts of people gathered around without delay. Many came uninvited just for feasting themselves freely, As the Patiala chief had started a lavish community kitchen. (35)
lines: Many other sycophants and distant relatives too arrived,
All sorts of people gathered around without delay.
Many came uninvited just for feasting themselves freely,
As the Patiala chief had started a lavish community kitchen.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As the Patiala chief made an inspection of his troops, After mounting his soldiers on horses in full battle gear, Highly arrogant did he feel as he inspected his troops, As this massive army stood ready on a vast area. (36)
lines: As the Patiala chief made an inspection of his troops,
After mounting his soldiers on horses in full battle gear,
Highly arrogant did he feel as he inspected his troops,
As this massive army stood ready on a vast area.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

A very loud roar arose with the beat of war drums, Four times larger than the Khalsa Dal did his army appear. Then as he inspected his battery of artillery guns, The whole sky was overcast as they fired those guns. (37)
lines: A very loud roar arose with the beat of war drums,
Four times larger than the Khalsa Dal did his army appear.
Then as he inspected his battery of artillery guns,
The whole sky was overcast as they fired those guns.

blocks.text: Thereafter, as he inspected the infantry soldiers, Extremely excited and proud did he feel. After ordering the artillery guns to open fire, Outside his fort did he get these guns deployed. (38)
lines: Thereafter, as he inspected the infantry soldiers,
Extremely excited and proud did he feel.
After ordering the artillery guns to open fire,
Outside his fort did he get these guns deployed.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Highly overjoyed did the Patiala chief feel after inspecting his troops, In a highly arrogant vein did he utter these remarks: Leave aside a single Khalsa Misl chief Baghel Singh, Even the whole Khalsa Panth force would get defeated. (39)
lines: Highly overjoyed did the Patiala chief feel after inspecting his troops,
In a highly arrogant vein did he utter these remarks: Leave aside a single Khalsa Misl chief Baghel Singh,
Even the whole Khalsa Panth force would get defeated.

blocks.text: He had his whole army under his single-hand command, Whereas Khalsa Panth force had too many commanders. Hearing this, the sycophants did burst out in applause, Never would he return home after suffering defeat. (40)
lines: He had his whole army under his single-hand command,
Whereas Khalsa Panth force had too many commanders.
Hearing this, the sycophants did burst out in applause,
Never would he return home after suffering defeat.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The intelligence gatherers whom the Patiala chief had sent secretly, The strength of S. Baghel Singh's force had they assessed. Four thousand musketeers had they reported in number, Who belonged to S. Baghel Singh's Misl alone. (41)
lines: The intelligence gatherers whom the Patiala chief had sent secretly,
The strength of S.
Baghel Singh's force had they assessed.
Four thousand musketeers had they reported in number,
Who belonged to S.
Baghel Singh's Misl alone.

blocks.text: As one thousand musketeers had joined from other Misls, Five thousand in total strength had they reported. There were many other hangers on who needed to be mentioned, Who had joined this force for the sake of plundering. (42)
lines: As one thousand musketeers had joined from other Misls,
Five thousand in total strength had they reported.
There were many other hangers on who needed to be mentioned,
Who had joined this force for the sake of plundering.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Hearing these news, delighted did S. Amar Singh feel, That he had a disciplined army under his command. As he had four times more troops under his command, Surely would he be able to capture S. Baghel Singh. (43)
lines: Hearing these news, delighted did S.
Amar Singh feel,
That he had a disciplined army under his command.
As he had four times more troops under his command,
Surely would he be able to capture S.
Baghel Singh.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Where could S. Baghel Singh flee, he remarked, Won't he be able to seek shelter in Majha or Delhi. Only five thousand horse-mounted cavalry he had, Whereas he (Amar Singh) commanded twelve thousand men. (44)
lines: Where could S.
Baghel Singh flee, he remarked,
Won't he be able to seek shelter in Majha or Delhi.
Only five thousand horse-mounted cavalry he had,
Whereas he (Amar Singh) commanded twelve thousand men.

blocks.text: No artillery guns did S. Baghel Singh possess, Whereas he (Amar Singh) possessed a large number of guns. Lavishly had he disbursed money among his troops, Whereas S. Baghel Singh's soldiers survived on loot and plunder. (45)
lines: No artillery guns did S.
Baghel Singh possess,
Whereas he (Amar Singh) possessed a large number of guns.
Lavishly had he disbursed money among his troops,
Whereas S.
Baghel Singh's soldiers survived on loot and plunder.

blocks.text: Hearing these reports, S. Dulcha Singh21 did feel highly concerned, Lest the Khalsa Panth forces should get defeated in battle. As such a massive force had S. Amar Singh gathered there, Lest he should disintegrate the Khalsa Panth force. (46)
lines: Hearing these reports,
S.
Dulcha Singh21 did feel highly concerned,
Lest the Khalsa Panth forces should get defeated in battle.
As such a massive force had S.
Amar Singh gathered there,
Lest he should disintegrate the Khalsa Panth force.

blocks.text: Dohra:

His (Dulcha Singh's) own territory being adjacent to Patiala state, Lest Amar Singh should annex his own territory. In that eventuality, how could he take back his area, Except after fighting a battle against the Malwa forces. (47)
lines: His (Dulcha Singh's) own territory being adjacent to Patiala state,
Lest Amar Singh should annex his own territory.
In that eventuality, how could he take back his area,
Except after fighting a battle against the Malwa forces.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

In a lighter vein did S. Baghel Singh tell S. Dulcha Singh, Nobody vacated an occupied territory without a fight. As S. Dulcha Singh apprehended lest they should be defeated, S. Baghel Singh would leave no stone unturned to win the battle. (48)
lines: In a lighter vein did S.
Baghel Singh tell S.
Dulcha Singh,
Nobody vacated an occupied territory without a fight.
As S.
Dulcha Singh apprehended lest they should be defeated,
S.
Baghel Singh would leave no stone unturned to win the battle.

blocks.text: As S. Baghel Singh ordered his troops to march towards Patiala, Highly incensed did S. Amar Singh feel at his rival's audacity. Instantly did he order his state troops to move forward, Must they seize all their horses after killing the Singhs. (49)
lines: As S.
Baghel Singh ordered his troops to march towards Patiala,
Highly incensed did S.
Amar Singh feel at his rival's audacity.
Instantly did he order his state troops to move forward,
Must they seize all their horses after killing the Singhs.

blocks.text: S. Chain Singh who had been S. Amar Singh's ambassador, He had been staying with S. Baghel Singh as S. Amar Singh's representative. Immediately did he send a couple of his deputies to S. Amar Singh, Never should S. Amar Singh fight against the Singhs underestimating their strength. (50)
lines: S.
Chain Singh who had been S.
Amar Singh's ambassador,
He had been staying with S.
Baghel Singh as S.
Amar Singh's representative.
Immediately did he send a couple of his deputies to S.
Amar Singh,
Never should S.
Amar Singh fight against the Singhs underestimating their strength.

blocks.text: (But) the Patiala chief accused him of using delaying tactics, A better opportunity than the present one would he never get. Thereafter, calling an assembly of hawks and Phulkian chiefs, He asked the opinion of his fraternity about the fight. (51)
lines: (But) the Patiala chief accused him of using delaying tactics,
A better opportunity than the present one would he never get.
Thereafter, calling an assembly of hawks and Phulkian chiefs,
He asked the opinion of his fraternity about the fight.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Whosoever considered himself wise among those invited, Immediate launching of an attack did they all advise. They accused the state advisor of joining the Singhs' camp, As he wished the Patiala chief to get defeated. (52)
lines: Whosoever considered himself wise among those invited,
Immediate launching of an attack did they all advise.
They accused the state advisor of joining the Singhs' camp,
As he wished the Patiala chief to get defeated.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

They insisted on fighting this battle on his behalf, Let him (S. Amar Singh) stay put in his Patiala fort. They bragged of capturing and presenting S. Baghel Singh alive, While the state ambassador wished to put off the fighting. (53)
lines: They insisted on fighting this battle on his behalf,
Let him (S.
Amar Singh) stay put in his Patiala fort.
They bragged of capturing and presenting S.
Baghel Singh alive,
While the state ambassador wished to put off the fighting.

blocks.text: He (S. Chain Singh) must have made a deal with the Singhs, Thus did the hawkish Phulkian chiefs allege. As destiny had ordained them to be doomed, Themselves were they inviting their own disaster. (54)
lines: He (S.
Chain Singh) must have made a deal with the Singhs,
Thus did the hawkish Phulkian chiefs allege.
As destiny had ordained them to be doomed,
Themselves were they inviting their own disaster.

blocks.text: Hearing this, the state ambassador once again advised, They must not move too far if they were bent upon fighting. At this remark, the people made him a butt of ridicule, That what a funny advisor had the Patiala chief employed. (55)
lines: Hearing this, the state ambassador once again advised,
They must not move too far if they were bent upon fighting.
At this remark, the people made him a butt of ridicule,
That what a funny advisor had the Patiala chief employed.

blocks.text: Thereafter, the hawks confabulated among themselves, Must they ransack the Singhs even without asking the king. Those who had never seen the Singhs fighting a battle, In vain did they sharpen their spears for a fight. (56)
lines: Thereafter, the hawks confabulated among themselves,
Must they ransack the Singhs even without asking the king.
Those who had never seen the Singhs fighting a battle,
In vain did they sharpen their spears for a fight.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The way these sons of Maj hails (from Majha), Had they, perchance, fallen into Phulkian forces hands that day, They would stab too many daggers, in their backs, As they would be fleeing the field on their horses and camels. (57)
lines: The way these sons of Maj hails (from Majha),
Had they, perchance, fallen into Phulkian forces hands that day,
They would stab too many daggers, in their backs,
As they would be fleeing the field on their horses and camels.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

A horse from the battle would he bring, dreamt someone, With fine leather strap would he leash the horse at home. On a most auspicious moment had he left home, said another, A treasure of his own choice would he bring home. (58)
lines: A horse from the battle would he bring, dreamt someone,
With fine leather strap would he leash the horse at home.
On a most auspicious moment had he left home, said another,
A treasure of his own choice would he bring home.

blocks.text: Still another had spotted a lion as he departed from home, A snake had been spotted by another, both being signs of violence. Those who had witnessed the Majhail Singhs fighting advised, The Malwai Singhs had better met their mothers before departure. (59)
lines: Still another had spotted a lion as he departed from home,
A snake had been spotted by another, both being signs of violence.
Those who had witnessed the Majhail Singhs fighting advised,
The Malwai Singhs had better met their mothers before departure.

blocks.text: They must embrace their mothers in case they have missed earlier, Who knows they may not return alive to meet their mothers. Indulging into such verbal pranks and loose talk, Did they try to spread such canards about the Majhail Singhs. (60)
lines: They must embrace their mothers in case they have missed earlier,
Who knows they may not return alive to meet their mothers.
Indulging into such verbal pranks and loose talk,
Did they try to spread such canards about the Majhail Singhs.

blocks.text: Now listen further to account of (Majhail) Singhs, As they heard about the large concentration of Malwa forces. With a sense of scare running across the Khalsa Dal ranks, Many among them attempted to send back their valuables. (61)
lines: Now listen further to account of (Majhail) Singhs,
As they heard about the large concentration of Malwa forces.
With a sense of scare running across the Khalsa Dal ranks,
Many among them attempted to send back their valuables.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Some felt that besides being smaller in number, Had they really been trapped in an alien land. In the event of state troops laying a siege around them, Hardly would they be able to break through the siege. (62)
lines: Some felt that besides being smaller in number,
Had they really been trapped in an alien land.
In the event of state troops laying a siege around them,
Hardly would they be able to break through the siege.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Though such being the sense of fear among the Khalsa ranks, But none did dare to share it with S. Baghel Singh. S. Dulcha Singh alone shared it with S. Baghel Singh, That the Malwais had concentrated in a large strength. (63)
lines: Though such being the sense of fear among the Khalsa ranks,
But none did dare to share it with S.
Baghel Singh.
S.
Dulcha Singh alone shared it with S.
Baghel Singh,
That the Malwais had concentrated in a large strength.

blocks.text: Neither had S. Baghel Singh sought assistance from another Misl, Nor had he consulted him (S. Dulcha Singh) being in haste, Now he must keep patience for five ten days, Thereafter, their Khalsa Dal force must beat a retreat. (64)
lines: Neither had S.
Baghel Singh sought assistance from another Misl,
Nor had he consulted him (S.
Dulcha Singh) being in haste,
Now he must keep patience for five ten days,
Thereafter, their Khalsa Dal force must beat a retreat.

blocks.text: At this S. Baghel Singh remarked in the same smiling vein, With what face would they retreat at that stage. As the Malwais would come after them in hot pursuit, Would their Misl not become a butt of ridicule among the Panth? (65)
lines: At this S.
Baghel Singh remarked in the same smiling vein,
With what face would they retreat at that stage.
As the Malwais would come after them in hot pursuit,
Would their Misl not become a butt of ridicule among the Panth?

blocks.text: Thereafter did S. Baghel Singh ordered the war drum to be beaten, So would it happen what the Divine Guru willed it to be. Calling an assembly of Misl chiefs, he held a congregation, At a resolution did they arrive to fight a battle. (66)
lines: Thereafter did S.
Baghel Singh ordered the war drum to be beaten,
So would it happen what the Divine Guru willed it to be.
Calling an assembly of Misl chiefs, he held a congregation,
At a resolution did they arrive to fight a battle.

blocks.text: Dohra:
The whole Khalsa Panth Misl agreed to obey, Whatever had been proposed by S. Baghel Singh. From fighting and being killed had they never shirked, As that had been their occupation everyday. (67)
lines: The whole Khalsa Panth Misl agreed to obey,
Whatever had been proposed by S.
Baghel Singh.
From fighting and being killed had they never shirked,
As that had been their occupation everyday.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereafter S. Dulcha Singh was made the chief commander, S Sukhu Singh22 was made to lead from the front. S. Shyam Singh Salinia, the Manimajra chief was taken along, Along with the chiefs of Rasulpur, Chola Sahib and Jhabbal. (68)
lines: Thereafter S.
Dulcha Singh was made the chief commander,
S Sukhu Singh22 was made to lead from the front.
S.
Shyam Singh Salinia, the Manimajra chief was taken along,
Along with the chiefs of Rasulpur,
Chola Sahib and Jhabbal.

blocks.text: As he deployed their forces on the right hand flank, The Kalsia chief's force was deployed on the left flank. Then S. Baghel Singh, exhorting all his chiefs, remarked, That the Misl's victory or defeat depended on their grit. (69)
lines: As he deployed their forces on the right hand flank,
The Kalsia chief's force was deployed on the left flank.
Then S.
Baghel Singh, exhorting all his chiefs, remarked,
That the Misl's victory or defeat depended on their grit.

blocks.text: As a few other Singh Misls also arrived to join them, They were asked to march with the main body. Must all of them remain alert and determined, Must they fight in the battle by wielding their swords. (70)
lines: As a few other Singh Misls also arrived to join them,
They were asked to march with the main body.
Must all of them remain alert and determined,
Must they fight in the battle by wielding their swords.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Moreover, the Singhs who had arrived from Doaba region, S. Baghel Singh kept those Singhs under his own command. Keeping their morale high through his repeated exhortations, He exhorted his troops to settle scores with the Malwais. (71)
lines: Moreover, the Singhs who had arrived from Doaba region,
S.
Baghel Singh kept those Singhs under his own command.
Keeping their morale high through his repeated exhortations,
He exhorted his troops to settle scores with the Malwais.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Another instruction did he pass to his chief commanders, Must all of them take their meals if not taken already. As the battle was likely to last for twenty four hours, A moment's rest would they not get till they won the battle. (72)
lines: Another instruction did he pass to his chief commanders,
Must all of them take their meals if not taken already.
As the battle was likely to last for twenty four hours,
A moment's rest would they not get till they won the battle.

blocks.text: The same instructions did the Singh chief's accept, All preparations for a twenty-four hours battle did they make. Moving their camps from the town of Ghanaur23 , The Khalsa force marched towards Patiala with their standards. (73)
lines: The same instructions did the Singh chief's accept,
All preparations for a twenty-four hours battle did they make.
Moving their camps from the town of Ghanaur23 ,
The Khalsa force marched towards Patiala with their standards.

blocks.text: As there rose a lot of din and noise with the beat of war drums, There spread a great/terrible panic around the city of Patiala. As rumours flew thick and fast from all the sides, The sun seemed to have been eclipsed by the rising dust. (74)
lines: As there rose a lot of din and noise with the beat of war drums,
There spread a great/terrible panic around the city of Patiala.
As rumours flew thick and fast from all the sides,
The sun seemed to have been eclipsed by the rising dust.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The Patiala chief (S. Amar Singh) observed the din and dust, From the ramparts of his fort where he sat. Ordering for the supply of ammunition to all his guns, He ordered his troops to get ready for the fight. (75)
lines: The Patiala chief (S.
Amar Singh) observed the din and dust,
From the ramparts of his fort where he sat.
Ordering for the supply of ammunition to all his guns,
He ordered his troops to get ready for the fight.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The king, making a royal official proclamation to wage a war, He ordered his troops to kill the Singhs and snatch their horses. Promising to reward the winners with robes and gold bracelets, He tried to boost the morale of his state troops. (76)
lines: The king, making a royal official proclamation to wage a war,
He ordered his troops to kill the Singhs and snatch their horses.
Promising to reward the winners with robes and gold bracelets,
He tried to boost the morale of his state troops.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Ordering the beating of drums loaded on horses and camels, Four times louder the din they raised than the Khalsa drums. As the sun got eclipsed by the rising din and dust, Difficult did it become to distinguish a friend from a foe. (77)
lines: Ordering the beating of drums loaded on horses and camels,
Four times louder the din they raised than the Khalsa drums.
As the sun got eclipsed by the rising din and dust,
Difficult did it become to distinguish a friend from a foe.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Looking at his massive force delighted did the king feel, Wrongly had his ambassador reported Khalsa forces strength. His own force being far greater in strength than the Khalsa force, Surely would his army defeat the Khalsa Dal force. (78)
lines: Looking at his massive force delighted did the king feel,
Wrongly had his ambassador reported Khalsa forces strength.
His own force being far greater in strength than the Khalsa force,
Surely would his army defeat the Khalsa Dal force.

blocks.text: His royal strike force did he order to make the first attack, Rest of his rural crowd did he keep near his fort. As the royal strike force confronted the Khalsa force, For a moment did it succeed in destabilising the Singhs. (79)
lines: His royal strike force did he order to make the first attack,
Rest of his rural crowd did he keep near his fort.
As the royal strike force confronted the Khalsa force,
For a moment did it succeed in destabilising the Singhs.

blocks.text: As both the sides mounted an attack on each other, The soldiers advanced, staggered, fell and stood up again. As Malwai soldiers attempted to hit with their daggers, The Singh musketeers fired at them to keep them at bay. (80)
lines: As both the sides mounted an attack on each other,
The soldiers advanced, staggered, fell and stood up again.
As Malwai soldiers attempted to hit with their daggers,
The Singh musketeers fired at them to keep them at bay.

blocks.text: Being trained in protecting themselves against a dagger attack, From a distance would the Singhs shoot at Malwa soldiers. With long-drawn swords as the state soldiers advanced, By firing bullets would the Singhs shoot them down. (81)
lines: Being trained in protecting themselves against a dagger attack,
From a distance would the Singhs shoot at Malwa soldiers.
With long-drawn swords as the state soldiers advanced,
By firing bullets would the Singhs shoot them down.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The best state soldiers who were mounted on their horses, To them also did the Singhs teach a good lesson. As these horse-mounted soldiers kept on attacking the Singhs, They, too, were shot down with bullets from their muskets. (82)
lines: The best state soldiers who were mounted on their horses,
To them also did the Singhs teach a good lesson.
As these horse-mounted soldiers kept on attacking the Singhs,
They, too, were shot down with bullets from their muskets.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Sudhrai who had Pathan soldiers under his command, Patiala chief asked him to attack the Singhs from the rear. As this Pathan contingent attacked the Khalsa force, S. Dulcha Singh's contingent rushed to block their passage. (83)
lines: Sudhrai who had Pathan soldiers under his command,
Patiala chief asked him to attack the Singhs from the rear.
As this Pathan contingent attacked the Khalsa force,
S.
Dulcha Singh's contingent rushed to block their passage.

blocks.text: As this Singh contingent also appeared to be over powered, S. Baghel Singh sent another contingent for his rescue. Some more soldiers did he despatch towards S. Sukhu Singh, As S. Baghel Singh noticed him coming under pressure. (84)
lines: As this Singh contingent also appeared to be over powered,
S.
Baghel Singh sent another contingent for his rescue.
Some more soldiers did he despatch towards S.
Sukhu Singh,
As S.
Baghel Singh noticed him coming under pressure.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Mightily did both the armies clash with each other, In high spirits and morale were both the combatants. Whosoever blinked and thought of retracing his steps first, In prestige and reputation would he lose indeed. (85)
lines: Mightily did both the armies clash with each other,
In high spirits and morale were both the combatants.
Whosoever blinked and thought of retracing his steps first,
In prestige and reputation would he lose indeed.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

For a couple of hours both the forces clashed so fiercely, That none did seem to be tracing their feet back. As the sharp weapons pierced and cut through their bodies, Much did they writhe and grieve in severe pain. (86)
lines: For a couple of hours both the forces clashed so fiercely,
That none did seem to be tracing their feet back.
As the sharp weapons pierced and cut through their bodies,
Much did they writhe and grieve in severe pain.

blocks.text: As the wounded Singhs kept sitting on the ground, The wounded Malwai soldiers rushed back to their camps. As four Malwai soldiers would withdraw carrying a single wounded man, The Singhs would taunt them for deserting the field. (87)
lines: As the wounded Singhs kept sitting on the ground,
The wounded Malwai soldiers rushed back to their camps.
As four Malwai soldiers would withdraw carrying a single wounded man,
The Singhs would taunt them for deserting the field.

blocks.text: Such being the will of providence that prevailed there, Malwa forces got uprooted on both the battle fronts. As Sukhu Singh went after the retreating force in hot pursuit, S. Dulcha Singh ordered the Khalsa force to push forward. (88)
lines: Such being the will of providence that prevailed there,
Malwa forces got uprooted on both the battle fronts.
As Sukhu Singh went after the retreating force in hot pursuit,
S.
Dulcha Singh ordered the Khalsa force to push forward.

blocks.text: As S. Baghel Singh ordered the camel-loaded war-drum beating, Gradually his Khalsa Panth force kept pushing the enemy back. As the Patiala chief observed the battle being lost, He brought forth the Rohela and hill chiefs infantry. (89)
lines: As S.
Baghel Singh ordered the camel-loaded war-drum beating,
Gradually his Khalsa Panth force kept pushing the enemy back.
As the Patiala chief observed the battle being lost,
He brought forth the Rohela and hill chiefs infantry.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Dashing and running some of them reached the battle front, A few odd shots did they try to fire from their muskets. Finding their own troops running and deserting the battlefield, They themselves could not hold the ground for long. (90)
lines: Dashing and running some of them reached the battle front,
A few odd shots did they try to fire from their muskets.
Finding their own troops running and deserting the battlefield,
They themselves could not hold the ground for long.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As the horse-mounted Patiala cavalry had deserted, The infantry troops came under a heavy attack. As only those who were nimble-footed could escape, The rest of them were dispossessed and brutally beaten. (91)
lines: As the horse-mounted Patiala cavalry had deserted,
The infantry troops came under a heavy attack.
As only those who were nimble-footed could escape,
The rest of them were dispossessed and brutally beaten.

blocks.text: Thus did the whole Patiala army rushed back to Patiala, The Fort gates did they shut after entering the fort. Some of them fell into wayside ditches as they deserted, In the ditches did they keep lying to save their lives. (92)
lines: Thus did the whole Patiala army rushed back to Patiala,
The Fort gates did they shut after entering the fort.
Some of them fell into wayside ditches as they deserted,
In the ditches did they keep lying to save their lives.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Then did the Patiala chief issued further orders, That the Khalsa Panth force be pounded by artillery-fire. So much smoke and darkness did engulf the area, That it became difficult to distinguish between friend and foe. (93)
lines: Then did the Patiala chief issued further orders,
That the Khalsa Panth force be pounded by artillery-fire.
So much smoke and darkness did engulf the area,
That it became difficult to distinguish between friend and foe.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The son of S. Mahan Singh died in this battle, S. Pakhar Singh also got wounded in this encounter. So many others were killed in this great battle, That recording their names would make this epic too large. (94)
lines: The son of S.
Mahan Singh died in this battle,
S.
Pakhar Singh also got wounded in this encounter.
So many others were killed in this great battle,
That recording their names would make this epic too large.

blocks.text: The two villages of Lehal and Bandugar in the vicinity of Patiala, These two were ransacked by the Khalsa Panth force. Thereupon, did S. Chain Singh (ambassador) approach Baghel Singh, Jumping ahead, he caught the reigns of S. Baghel Singh's horse. (95)
lines: The two villages of Lehal and Bandugar in the vicinity of Patiala,
These two were ransacked by the Khalsa Panth force.
Thereupon, did S.
Chain Singh (ambassador) approach Baghel Singh,
Jumping ahead, he caught the reigns of S.
Baghel Singh's horse.

blocks.text: He pleaded with Baghel Singh to put an end to fighting, As ten times more had his forces beaten the Patiala force. S. Dulcha Singh also arrived to persuade S. Baghel Singh, That he must not take any more risk after this victory. (96)
lines: He pleaded with Baghel Singh to put an end to fighting,
As ten times more had his forces beaten the Patiala force.
S.
Dulcha Singh also arrived to persuade S.
Baghel Singh,
That he must not take any more risk after this victory.

blocks.text: Thereupon, S. Baghel ordered his army to retreat, After planting his flags on the land of those two villages. He sent back the ambassador with the instructions, That the Patiala chief must stop the artillery firing. (97)
lines: Thereupon,
S.
Baghel ordered his army to retreat,
After planting his flags on the land of those two villages.
He sent back the ambassador with the instructions,
That the Patiala chief must stop the artillery firing.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Then did S. Chain Singh tell the Patiala chief, With folded hands did he humbly submit. He had already conveyed in writing to Patiala chief, Never should he fight the Khalsa, be they in minority. (98)
lines: Then did S.
Chain Singh tell the Patiala chief,
With folded hands did he humbly submit.
He had already conveyed in writing to Patiala chief,
Never should he fight the Khalsa, be they in minority.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Guru's power is vested in the Khalsa Panth, Khalsa Panth abounds in sages and savants. Khalsa Panth is known for its emblems of war, Patiala chief's ancestors had acknowledged Panth's superiority. (99)
lines: Guru's power is vested in the Khalsa Panth,
Khalsa Panth abounds in sages and savants.
Khalsa Panth is known for its emblems of war,
Patiala chief's ancestors had acknowledged Panth's superiority.

blocks.text: (But) Patiala ruler favoured recruiting more troops, More funds did he plan to bring from Bathinda treasury. A lot of money did he wish to spend on recruitment, With money did he wish to cause divisions in Khalsa Panth. (100)
lines: (But) Patiala ruler favoured recruiting more troops,
More funds did he plan to bring from Bathinda treasury.
A lot of money did he wish to spend on recruitment,
With money did he wish to cause divisions in Khalsa Panth.

blocks.text: It was by chance that his army got defeated, he alleged, His army had deserted the battlefield in his absence. A few more Khalsa contingents should he invite in his support, The Khalsa contingents which were bigger than S. Baghel Singh's Misl. (101)
lines: It was by chance that his army got defeated, he alleged,
His army had deserted the battlefield in his absence.
A few more Khalsa contingents should he invite in his support,
The Khalsa contingents which were bigger than S.
Baghel Singh's Misl.

blocks.text: Then did S. Chain Singh remark after a thorough analysis, How could he dare to cause divisions in the Khalsa Panth. Both Majhail and Malwai Singhs constituted a Singh fraternity, Both had been ransacking inner and outer territories together. (102)
lines: Then did S.
Chain Singh remark after a thorough analysis,
How could he dare to cause divisions in the Khalsa Panth.
Both Majhail and Malwai Singhs constituted a Singh fraternity,
Both had been ransacking inner and outer territories together.

blocks.text: There were always two sides to a fight, One combatant won the field the other got defeated. Many a time had Patiala forces defeated the Khalsa, Many a time had they been defeated by the Khalsa. (103)
lines: There were always two sides to a fight,
One combatant won the field the other got defeated.
Many a time had Patiala forces defeated the Khalsa,
Many a time had they been defeated by the Khalsa.

blocks.text: Dohra:

There are four accepted strategies in politics, These strategies being 'Saam', 'Daam', 'Dand' and 'Bhaid'24. The enemy can be driven out from one's country, By using anyone or all of these strategies one by one. (104)
lines: There are four accepted strategies in politics,
These strategies being 'Saam',
'Daam',
'Dand' and 'Bhaid'24.
The enemy can be driven out from one's country,
By using anyone or all of these strategies one by one.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Declaring S. Chain Singh to be a wise counsellor, The Patiala ruler promised to follow his advice. Thereafter, did S. Chain Singh return to the Khalsa Panth, Instantly did he return the occupied territory to the Khalsa. (105)
lines: Declaring S.
Chain Singh to be a wise counsellor,
The Patiala ruler promised to follow his advice.
Thereafter, did S.
Chain Singh return to the Khalsa Panth,
Instantly did he return the occupied territory to the Khalsa.

blocks.text: Whatever desirable ransom and revenues accrued to the Khalsa, The whole amount did he handover to the Singhs. The other Singh Misls who had come in support, These two were compensated with ransom and revenues. (106)
lines: Whatever desirable ransom and revenues accrued to the Khalsa,
The whole amount did he handover to the Singhs.
The other Singh Misls who had come in support,
These two were compensated with ransom and revenues.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The same day did S. Baghel Singh depart from there, After resolving all the issues and revenues of his Misl. With great pomp and show did he turn back, After collecting all the ransom and the revenues. (107)
lines: The same day did S.
Baghel Singh depart from there,
After resolving all the issues and revenues of his Misl.
With great pomp and show did he turn back,
After collecting all the ransom and the revenues.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereupon, did S. Chain Singh ponder over the whole situation, There had not been any harmonious reconciliation between the two chiefs. As S. Baghel Singh was believed to be a great strategist, Lest he should devise a plan to harm the Patiala chief. (108)
lines: Thereupon, did S.
Chain Singh ponder over the whole situation,
There had not been any harmonious reconciliation between the two chiefs.
As S.
Baghel Singh was believed to be a great strategist,
Lest he should devise a plan to harm the Patiala chief.

blocks.text: S. Baghel Singh had remarked while mounting his steed, That S. Amar Singh had not cared to meet him. Thereupon, the Patiala chief did beseech S. Chain Singh to stop him, That he must bring about reconcilliation between them. (109)
lines: S.
Baghel Singh had remarked while mounting his steed,
That S.
Amar Singh had not cared to meet him.
Thereupon, the Patiala chief did beseech S.
Chain Singh to stop him,
That he must bring about reconcilliation between them.

blocks.text: Thereupon, S. Chain Singh approached S. Baghel Singh and told, That S. Amar Singh was on his way to see him as he departed. As S. Baghel Singh somewhat frowned upon this belated move, Instantly did S. Chain Singh catch hold of the reigns of Singh's horse. (110)
lines: Thereupon,
S.
Chain Singh approached S.
Baghel Singh and told,
That S.
Amar Singh was on his way to see him as he departed.
As S.
Baghel Singh somewhat frowned upon this belated move,
Instantly did S.
Chain Singh catch hold of the reigns of Singh's horse.

blocks.text: Thus did S. Chain Singh escort S. Baghel Singh to the Patiala chief, Once again did he present many gifts to S. Baghel Singh. Patiala chief's son whom his father had taken along with himself, Him did he offer to Baghel Singh for adoption. (Ill)
Dohra:

As the young prince was made a Singh after initiation, A close family bond got established between the two. Thereafter, many a favour did S. Baghel Singh shower, On the Patiala chief in quick succession of each other. (112)
lines: As the young prince was made a Singh after initiation,
A close family bond got established between the two.
Thereafter, many a favour did S.
Baghel Singh shower,
On the Patiala chief in quick succession of each other.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Whenever any other Misl cast an evil eye on the Patiala chief, Instantly would S. Baghel Singh rush to rally round him. Dearer than his own Misl did he regard the Patiala State, Even as S. Amar Singh valued his support extremely. (113)
lines: Whenever any other Misl cast an evil eye on the Patiala chief,
Instantly would S.
Baghel Singh rush to rally round him.
Dearer than his own Misl did he regard the Patiala State,
Even as S.
Amar Singh valued his support extremely.

blocks.text: The moment S. Amar Singh, the Patiala ruler, breathed his last, The same moment did other Misl chiefs occupy his territory. As Singhpuria Misl25 occupied the Banur area of Patiala, S. Sangat Singh's Misl occupied the area of village Mulaiypur. (114)
lines: The moment S.
Amar Singh, the Patiala ruler, breathed his last,
The same moment did other Misl chiefs occupy his territory.
As Singhpuria Misl25 occupied the Banur area of Patiala,
S.
Sangat Singh's Misl occupied the area of village Mulaiypur.

blocks.text: As the Patiala State was encroached upon from all sides, The power of the Patiala chief's Sahib Singh26 declined very low. As his enemies invited the Marhattas to occupy his territory, S. Baghel Singh turned them out after a good fight. (115)
lines: As the Patiala State was encroached upon from all sides,
The power of the Patiala chief's Sahib Singh26 declined very low.
As his enemies invited the Marhattas to occupy his territory,
S.
Baghel Singh turned them out after a good fight.

blocks.text: Thereafter, as Dewan Nanu Mai27 defied the Patiala chief, S. Baghel Singh turned him out after confiscating his property. Thereafter, as the Bhattis ransacked the Patiala state, S. Baghel Singh arrived and killed all the invaders. (116)
lines: Thereafter, as Dewan Nanu Mai27 defied the Patiala chief,
S.
Baghel Singh turned him out after confiscating his property.
Thereafter, as the Bhattis ransacked the Patiala state,
S.
Baghel Singh arrived and killed all the invaders.

blocks.text: Boha and Budhladha which were occupied were vacated, From Sirsa and Rania were the Bhattis evicted. Thereafter, sending his force for collecting land revenues, They collected revenues from the eight villages of Hansi and Hissar. (117)
lines: Boha and Budhladha which were occupied were vacated,
From Sirsa and Rania were the Bhattis evicted.
Thereafter, sending his force for collecting land revenues,
They collected revenues from the eight villages of Hansi and Hissar.

blocks.text: Dohra:

What more should the author narrate about such a person, Who devoted his whole life to uphold the family bondage. Such are those great personages who keep their word, In order to honour and uphold their solemn pledges. (118)
lines: What more should the author narrate about such a person,
Who devoted his whole life to uphold the family bondage.
Such are those great personages who keep their word,
In order to honour and uphold their solemn pledges.
